facts.statement: The species Linxiavis inaquosus was described by Li et al. in 2020.
The description of Linxiavis was based on articulated and associated fossil elements including wings, shoulder girdle, vertebrae, and hind limbs.
facts.quote: Linxiavis was described in 2020 on the basis of articulated and associated elements of the wings, shoulder girdle, vertebrae, and hind limb

facts.statement: The fossil exhibits specific traits of Columbiformes and Sandgrouses, including a notarium and a short coracoid shaft.
facts.quote: that exhibited apomorphies of Columbiformes and Sandgrouses (Pteroclidae) such as a notarium, and a short coracoid shaft.

facts.statement: The holotype suggests that sandgrouse like Linxiavis may have continuously occupied arid, high-elevation Tibetan habitats since the late Miocene, carrying water in modified breast feathers to feed their young.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil suggests that the arid and high elevation Tibetan habitats may have been continuously occupied since the late Miocene by sandgrouse that would've been carrying water in their modified breast feathers to their young.

facts.statement: Linxiavis belongs to the family Pteroclidae.
Linxiavis lived during the Tortonian to Messinian stages, between 11.63 and 5.333 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Messinian (11.63 to 5.333 million years ago)
